newsitem.title: SWEDEN: RALLYING-ERIKSSON LEADS MCRAE AFTER DAY-LONG BATTLE.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-ERIKSSON LEADS MCRAE AFTER DAY-LONG BATTLE.

text.p: Swede Kenneth Eriksson won a day-long battle with Subaru team-mate Briton Colin McRae and world champion Finn Tommi Makinen to lead the Swedish Rally at the end of the second day in Borlange on Saturday.

In a hard-fought tussle between the top four contenders, Eriksson took the lead on the fourth stage from Spaniard Carlos Sainz, lost it briefly to Makinen after the sixth stage, but regained it after an impressive performance on the 45km long Jutbo eighth and penultimate stage.
McRae, who ended the day just seven seconds behind Eriksson despite a spin on the fourth stage, believed that the Subaru team's choice of tyres played a key factor in their performance.
"We've fared well against the opposition because Pirelli have done a lot of work with the team and we are prepared for any conditions," the Scot said.

Makinen, who drives for Mitsubishi, was in an untroubled third place, 20 seconds behind McRae. Sainz was three seconds further adrift in fourth, despite having earlier caused minor damage to his car on the second stage in a spin.
The drivers' main worries now return to the weather, with new snow falls expected on the third day and likely to hide icy conditions.
